title: oncall: weighted-priority sampling for autodiagnostics suggestions
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Add weighted-priority sampling to the incident-bot autodiagnostics suggestions pipeline to surface higher-confidence runbooks and replicable diagnostics during on-call. Motivation: on recent incidents we observed noisy autodiagnostic suggestions where low-confidence items cluttered the on-call view and delayed triage. This change introduces a priority weight model derived from SLO impact, recent runbook success rate, and heuristic relevancy signals from the SLO toolkit. The PR includes a new sampling module, backfill migration for recent suggestion scores, telemetry for sampling decisions, and an opt-in feature flag for staged rollout. Checklist: 1) implement weighted sampler and unit tests; 2) integrate with existing oncall suggestion flow; 3) add metrics and logs; 4) docs for runbook authors and oncall; 5) feature flag + canary rollout plan. Related: ENG-3245 (autodiag quality improvements), SUP-4312 (customer SLO escalations). No breaking API changes. Behavior: defaults to safe conservative sampling (min weight floor) and a quick opt-out via flags for teams during canary. The feature will be rolled out to 10% of teams for 48h, then 50%, then 100% after monitoring stable.

release_notes: Improve autodiagnostics suggestion ordering by adding weighted-priority sampling that boosts higher-confidence runbooks and diagnostics. Feature gated and rolled out via canary. Observability added for sampling decisions.
summary: Implements weighted sampling in incident-bot to surface higher-quality autodiagnostics to on-call engineers, adds metrics, docs, tests, and a canary rollout plan.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover edge cases (zero weights, ties, deterministic seeding). Canary run included synthetic incidents to validate suggestion ranking; telemetry validated sampling.reason and sampling.swap_count. No regressions observed in oncall flow during 48h canary at 10%.
rollback_plan: Feature flag can be disabled per-team via config; a global kill-switch is available in the incident-bot control plane. If metrics show increased false positives, rollback to prior sampler and roll forward fixes.
deployment_plan: Stage: 10% teams for 48h -> 50% teams for 24h -> 100% after stable metrics. Monitor sampling.swap_count, suggestion_apdex, and oncall_feedback.survey for regressions.
authors_notes: This change is intentionally conservative: weights are normalized and a floor prevents starvation. Follow-up work: add ML-derived relevancy score integration (ENG-3310).
